question: Which among the following was NOT a part of the ancient supercontinent called Gondwanaland?
solution:
The correct answer is__** France**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Gondwanaland was a vast ancient supercontinent that existed during the Late Paleozoic and Early Mesozoic eras, approximately **600 million to 180 million years ago**.
 
• The supercontinent included landmasses that are now part of several continents, such as **South Africa, India, and Australia**.
 
• France, being located in the northern hemisphere, was part of the supercontinent Laurasia, which formed in conjunction with Gondwanaland.
 
• The breakup of Gondwanaland led to the formation of modern continents and significantly influenced the geological and biological evolution of the Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Components of Gondwanaland**: Gondwanaland included several major landmasses, including present-day **Africa, South America, Antarctica, India, and Australia.**
 
• **Geological Significance**: The study of Gondwanaland helps scientists understand plate tectonics, continental drift, and the historical climate change.
 
• Gondwanaland collided with Laurasia in the late Paleozoic era, which led to the formation of the Variscan mountain range.
